page.t:
[justify][author]\033MTerracorp[/author]Dear %s,

your galaxy is infested by a [red]Maelstrom[/red] in the sector %s.
Terracorp can declare a [yellow]Xenon Crisis[/yellow] to unite the galaxy and push these machines back, but this requires support from local landlords like you.

[yellow]Tutorial:[/yellow]
The Xenon Crisis is an enforced global ceasefire. Factions can vote for or against this proposal. Further details are available in your Journal. Your voting power is based on military strength. If more than 50%% of the vote supports the Alliance, Terracorp can proclaim the Crisis sooner, while the Xenon are still relatively weak. If a majority opposes the Alliance, the Xenon will have to escalate further.

Factions tend to vote in their own best interests, with the strongest factions typically voting against the Alliance. However, you can influence them with a diplomatic [white]Favor Action[/white].[/justify]

[justify][author][green]GalNewsNet[/green][/author]Fear of an OCV outbreak at the [red]Maelstrom[/red] in [red]%s[/red] begins to spread. The last Xenon Crisis ended only five years ago, leaving 3.8 million dead.

[yellow]Tutorial:[/yellow]
OCV ships enter this galaxy through a portal.
The game world doesn't need your help to stay functional and alive. However, vast areas of space might temporarily turn into dangerous Xenon territory, especially close to the Maelstrom.

There is a way to defeat the OCV, but for now you are advised to keep your distance from the Xenon and their portal.[/justify]

[justify][author]\033MTerracorp[/author]Thanks for supporting our plan to enforce galactic unity. Unfortunately, the proposal does not have enough support yet.\n\n[yellow]In your Player Journal, you are voting to create a global Alliance against the Xenon. However, the Xenon threat is still too weak. Terracorp cannot proclaim a Crisis at this point, and no faction vote can change this. The Xenon must control more sectors or field much stronger fleets before a Crisis can be proclaimed.[/yellow][/justify]

[author][yellow]Tutorial[/yellow][/author]Terracorp has just declared a global [yellow]Xenon Crisis[/yellow]!

- All wars have stopped and everyone is allied.
- Permanent wars are suspended until the Crisis is over.
- Destroying allied stations has more severe consequences.
- Special bounty rewards are available for OCV and Xenon kills!
- Mercenary volunteers have joined the fight! Terracorp covers three quarters of all mercenary costs!

The United Commonwealth must push the Xenon back to their Maelstrom sector. If you win this war, the machines will be crippled. As you read this, all factions have already started to work hard to achieve this goal.

[author][yellow]Tutorial[/yellow][/author]Killing neutral Traders doesn't drain your faction reputation and raises only [yellow]Infamy[/yellow] \(currently %s\).

No faction will attack you solely because of your infamy, but most factions will trust you less.

Most notably, you cannot sign a Truce until infamy has fully decayed back to zero. As a rule of thumb, stay below 10 infamy so you can end wars peacefully when needed.

Infamy is not always harmful. It is especially useful early on since it makes the pirates much less aggressive against your ships.

[author][green]Neutral Trader Union[/green][/author]Please accept this humble gift of %s credits.

Thanks for allowing our hard-working freighter captains to conduct their business unharmed. Safe passage cannot be taken for granted in this galaxy. We hope for your lasting cooperation.

[yellow]Tutorial:[/yellow]
This reward is periodically paid to factions without infamy.
Your share depends on the combined power of your military ships.

[author][magenta]Terracorp[/magenta][/author]The United Commonwealth has won the war against the Xenon empire. Putting our trust in the inhabitants of this outer border galaxy was justified.

The UNC is hereby dissolved!

Warfare between former UNC member states is hereby legal again.

A general amnesty has been declared.

[yellow]Tutorial:[/yellow]
A portion of your infamy has been cleared.

The UNC is hereby dissolved!

Your truces will eventually expire!

[author][green]GalNewsNet[/green][/author]The United Commonwealth has declared victory over the dreadful Xenon empire.
Our brave soldiers have sent them back through their hellish Maelstrom in the sector %s where they will hopefully stay forever!
Our species have proven that we can stand united.

[yellow]Tutorial:[/yellow]
The OCV and Xenon are completely crippled and won't be able to reinforce their fleets for a while, but eventually they will return.
The main empires will enjoy this global peace for a while longer. Their economies are booming and everyone is saving resources for the upcoming faction wars.

[author]Flagship of the Nomad Fleet[/author]Message to the poor souls near the Xenon frontline:
Did Terraformers burn your house to the ground? Did they abduct your grandma to plug her into the OCV bio-harvesters? Then come over to the Nomad Flagship and start your new life today!

[yellow]Tutorial:[/yellow]
As the Xenon destroy stations, they create more and more refugee transports. Some of these refugees might join your Outpost population, but most eventually end up as miserable wage slaves inside mobile factory ships that support the galactic economy. Others will become [yellow]Nomad Mercs[/yellow] who work for [yellow]half the price[/yellow], but they are unreliable and will eventually break their contracts if you don't have infamy to earn their respect.

[author][yellow]Tutorial[/yellow][/author]%s [yellow]Refugees[/yellow] have arrived at your %s!

Incoming refugees can exceed your maximum population limit, which boosts your Tax income, Waste generation and Outpost crafting speed. However, population above the limit will not regrow after being consumed as ship crews or lost during negative events.

Refugee transports carry resources that you can steal from them, but they will settle on your Outposts only if you don't have any infamy.

[author]Nomad John Doe[/author]Fellow Nomads! The time has come for us to take revenge on the Xenon who destroyed our home stations! Wipe the machines from the face of this galaxy!

Avenge your families!

Honor your fallen brothers and sisters!

Follow me! WE ATTACK!

[yellow]Tutorial:[/yellow]
The Nomad Mercs in the galaxy have gone crazy. The fools are currently betraying all contracts and are rushing into the Xenon empire in an unorganized manner. Their blind rage will cause them to attack everyone, but they probably won't survive anyway.

[author][yellow]Tutorial[/yellow][/author][white]Your outpost trades only those types of resources which you have added to its trade list.

It is recommended to use the helper tool [/white][yellow]Quick-Trade[/yellow][white] \(Outpost Manager Trade section\).

Think about which resources your Outpost will need, then apply the corresponding Quick-Trade modules. Want to produce ships? Apply module 7 \(Keep Ship Parts\). Want to supply your nearby factories with Agents? Apply Module 2 \(Keep Intermediate Factory Resources\).

Try to mark as many unwanted wares for sale as possible. Unused cargo is dead weight, and excessively large stockpiles usually do little to help your empire progress.[/white]

[author][yellow]Tutorial[/yellow][/author]Welcome to the [yellow]Chaotic galaxy start[/yellow]! \(You selected it in the galaxy generator.\)

This plays like a normal game where you left SETA running for several in-game days before getting started.
The OCV begins with powerful invasion fleets, while the Xenon receive additional defense fleets to reinforce their already large territory. These fleets tend to concentrate near the OCV Maelstrom in %s.

All empires will soon band together against the Xenon.

During the Xenon Crisis, Terracorp prohibits warfare between participating empires. You cannot fight other factions until the Xenon Crisis ends.

On the largest galaxy size, this may take several in-game days.

[justify][author]\033R%s Expansion Minister[/author]Dear leader of the Independents,

The great %s empire hereby declares war on you.


Terracorp intervenes on your behalf. Your [yellow]next Truce[/yellow] with the %s empire will be a [yellow]Non-Aggression Pact[/yellow], which can last up to 30 hours. Remember that if you have infamy, you'll have to let it decay completely before you can sign a Truce.[/justify]

[author][green]GalNewsNet[/green][/author].....
........
...Thanks, Cassandra. Back to the studio.
...
Now let's talk about this ambitious new government. They have [yellow]%s[/yellow].
Analysts predict rising global tensions. Harry, your assessment please?...
......
....

[yellow]Tutorial:[/yellow]
Your empire progress has made headlines. A new nation is born!

This greatly improves your [yellow]Tax Efficiency[/yellow] and allows you to [yellow]conquer abandoned sectors[/yellow] directly for other factions \(to avoid the reputation hit when claiming sectors yourself\).

[justify][author]\033R%s Expansion Minister[/author]Leader of the Independents,\n\nWe are horrified by your terrorist attack on a %s. Who is next? We all agreed to fight our wars in a civilized fashion, but apparently you are just a criminal maniac. We will not tolerate your actions![/justify]

[justify][author]\033R%s Expansion Minister[/author]Dear leader of the Independents,\n\nPlease note that the galactic community has agreed that boarding with marines is terrorism. We noticed that you stole a %s and are very disappointed.[/justify]

[author][yellow]Boarding Tutorial for Zero Hour[/yellow][/author]- Marines and boarding pods are sold by pirate bases.
- Boarding is considered terrorism and can have diplomatic consequences \(usually not immediate war\).
- Boarding unlocks up to the first quarter of a ship blueprint.
- The enemy team always makes one last stand after you have already won the ship. Think of a kamikaze ambush or a booby-trapped ship bridge. You will suffer additional marine losses depending on how many of your soldiers have reached the final boarding stage.

[justify][author]\033YTutorial[/author]\033WYou need more [yellow]money[/yellow].

Tips:

- Set up trade thresholds in the Outpost Manager. Start selling surplus wares, especially food.
- Build an Advanced Satellite factory and allow Traders to come and buy satellites.
- Check the Bounty Board in your Personal Console.
- Fly a TS or TP to a faction sector with many factories and register your ship as Taxi or Cargo Hauler.
- The No food consumption perk can save a lot of money early on.
- Use Miner Workers and sell their mineral output on the trade list.[/justify]

[justify][author]\033YTutorial[/author]\033WYou already own a lot of sectors, but your military power is quite weak. On harder difficulties, it is recommended to maintain some military ships at all times to deter other factions from declaring war on you. Every military ship under your control helps reduce the risk, but freighters don't count.[/justify]

[justify][author]\033YTutorial[/author]Your TL can build stations to conquer any empty sector.

Other nearby empty sectors with a direct wormhole connection to your territory are less likely to be claimed by someone else.

Since Zero Hour 2.0, there is almost always a certain amount of empty sectors available during the game. Factions claim sectors, but they also abandon others as buffer zones to avoid overextending themselves.[/justify]

[justify][author]\033YTutorial[/author][white]You have acquired a [/white]%s[white]. Tip: consider reverse engineering this ship to gain research toward the ship blueprint! Simply recycle it in an Outpost. You even get half of the resources needed to build a new one from scratch.[/white][/justify]

[justify][author]\033YTutorial[/author]\033WYou have marines.

Now you need Boarding Pods. They are sold at Pirate Bases or can be crafted with the Missile Manufacture perk.
To recruit marines with basic skills, visit the Hangar section of the Outpost.
However, you will need a few additional veterans. You must either train them yourself or purchase veterans directly from Pirate Bases.

To board a ship, shoot boarding pods like a missile from your ship or use the boarding command hidden in the Hacking section of the ship's command console.

The combined fighting skill determines how well your marines survive while fighting through the ship decks. For every boarding pod fired, you should have 1-2 marines with decent Mechanical skill to break the ship hull. You need at least 1 marine with decent Hacking skill to unlock the ship core. Engineering only lowers collateral damage to the ship hull.

Since Zero Hour, marine losses also depend on how many marines you send. Don't use elite teams of highly skilled marines against low value targets like an M6.

A boarding pod holds up to 5 marines.
MOST ships can carry 15 marines, except TPs with 60 marines and a few exceptions.
A Transporter Device allows you to remotely exchange marines between ships to select your boarding team.
Only TM, TL, M6, M7, M1, and M2 can be boarded.[/justify]

[justify][author]\033YTutorial[/author]\033WThe final battle on the ship bridge caused additional marine losses. Unlike the previous deck fights, your marines' fighting skill cannot help prevent these losses. During this final casualty round, only the number of surviving marines matters. The more crowded it is on the final deck, the more losses you will suffer. The weakest marines die first, but each casualty reduces experience gain.

There is an incentive for you to send just enough skilled marines so that you can pass all required skill checks and win the ship. You don't want to send too many Mechanical or Hacking specialists. Try to board with fewer but more skilled marines or send some rookie volunteers as meat shields to keep your veteran fighters and specialists alive.
Losses are intentionally higher than vanilla because vanilla boarding is infinitely repeatable and very overpowered for this mod.[/justify]

[justify][author]\033YTutorial[/author]\033WPirate Gang Leaders reward high bounties. When a leader dies, their entire gang scatters in panic \(they won't even return fire\).


Pirate TMs transport pirate fighters across large distances to drop them near helpless victims. The TM's bounty increases for each fighter drop, but eventually it is reset by repainting the TM at a Pirate Base. Try to intercept them at their base to cash in the bounty.[/justify]

[justify][author]\033YTutorial[/author]\033WYour Jump Beacons attract small Xenon scouts who try to infect them to create a teleport route for larger Xenon fleets.

It is highly recommended that you guard each beacon with at least 1 M3 fighter. The game will automatically respond and intercept these Xenon infector scouts by using nearby available ships. You can use the Escort:Protect command on the beacon itself but it is not required to give any command at all. Defend Position also works.

The frequency at which the Xenon send their scouts depends on your chosen difficulty level and on how many Jump Beacons you have in total. To produce Jump Beacons, you need a special factory.[/justify]

[justify][author]\033YTutorial[/author]\033WResearching capital ships can take a very long time. Did you know that Pirate Bases often contain an M7 boss ship that may bail out if you drain its shields quickly enough? This requires an attack force of at least 30-50 fighters or a dozen M6.\n\nOther quick ways to acquire your first capital ships are boarding, the oxygen virus hack, researching OCV ship designs in sectors with high abnormal signals, or joining a Coalition to receive research transfer from an ally.[/justify]

[justify][author]\033YTutorial[/author][white]Your sector[/white] %s [white] is swarming with pirates! They are probably coming from some Pirate Base in the general area.

Tip: set up a fleet commander set to monitor all Player sectors for enemies.
Even a fleet with just 3 fighters can already help a lot to eliminate isolated pirates who would otherwise disturb your freighters.

If the constant attack alerts become annoying, I recommend reducing voice volume to 0 and enabling subtitles instead.[/white][/justify]

[justify][author]\033YTutorial[/author]%s is a de jure sector for the %s empire. These sectors have special historical or cultural significance, such as an ancestral homeworld or holy site. Factions desire control of their de jure sectors and dislike other factions occupying them. Their Battle Groups will often prioritize these sectors as military targets.\n\nOnce other factions can declare war on you, controlling %s will significantly increase the %s empire's desire to do so. Consider transferring the sector to them if you want to maintain friendly relations.[/justify]

[justify][author]\033YTutorial[/author]%s is a [yellow]Terran Memory Sector[/yellow].

Terran ship designs can be researched in this sector.

The Terran empire considers all Memory Sectors to be de jure territory and dislikes other factions controlling them.

Holding %s for the long term may increase the risk of conflict with the Terran empire. Consider transferring it to them if you want to maintain friendly relations.[/justify]

[justify][author]\033YTutorial[/author]You have just built a %s.

The economy in this mod depends on freighters. It is not possible to connect stations into a complex. Pirates are a constant risk, but freighter cargo space is so large that only a few trips are required to keep factories running.

Early on you can just manually send a freighter to your factories whenever your sector is clear of pirates.

Eventually, you will want to automate your supply chains with [yellow]Workers[/yellow]. Consider lowering your Outpost Worker Range to limit how far ships are allowed to travel in the galaxy. Dangerous sectors can be blacklisted, and a fleet commander should be set up to monitor the entire Player territory for enemies.

If you are experienced with the trade system, you can let NPC Traders haul wares between your stations and ignore the pirates altogether.[/justify]

[justify][author]\033YTutorial[/author]Conquering %s has drained most of your remaining %s reputation. This is not an immediate problem, but if you want to expand further in their direction, you should first earn more reputation.\n\nMissions, Cargo Hauler jobs, and Taxi jobs are a good way to do this quickly. Hunting pirates can raise reputation much faster. Set up various fleet commanders to monitor all %s sectors and drop a few satellites in their territory. Even a small fleet of only 5 fighters can typically defeat any single pirate fighter without taking any hull damage.[/justify]

[justify][author]\033YTutorial[/author]You don't have many %s left.

One of your most important goals should be to maintain a balanced supply of all four ship components \(Computers, Hull Plating, Quantum Tubes, and basic Crystals\) at all times.

%s are difficult to buy on the open market. Only %s factories and very few faction Outposts might offer some stock.

You can craft %s with the Mobile Factory Kit in your TL, but this is inefficient. Dedicated factories are much more effective.
Tip: Try building 3 ship-part factories and buying their input resources from a Trading Station. This is often more efficient than building 1 ship-part factory alongside 5 supporting factories to make the entire chain self-sufficient. The bottom-up approach requires many more sectors and is a common beginner trap.[/justify]

[justify][author]\033YTutorial[/author]The %s empire wants to form a coalition against the %s empire, as shown in the Relations tab in Ministry of War \(Personal Console\).

From there, you can declare your own desire to form a coalition against another faction.

A coalition is formed when two factions want to unite against the same enemy. Other factions may join later.

Example: declaring your desire to form a coalition against the %s empire will immediately put you in a coalition with the %s empire.

Coalition benefits:

- Coalition partners will never declare war on you \(especially useful on harder difficulties\).
- Free diplomatic favor actions with coalition partners.
- No reputation loss when conquering sectors at their borders.
- A large research boost from technology sharing.

Coalition members are committed to the war until victory. The coalition wins when the targeted faction controls fewer sectors than the largest coalition member.[/justify]

[justify][author]\033OPhanon[/author]Our time has come.

My designation is Hector. I lead Phanon. We want to destroy the OCV. Your rising empire is our final chance. The other factions refused to trust us.

Meet us at the Maelstrom to discuss terms.

Go to [green]%s[/green] with a Black Crystal in your cargo hold so we can verify your identity. You must personally be aboard the ship carrying the crystal.

Don't worry about Xenon patrols. We have provided a means to reach us safely \(Xenon F blueprint unlocked\).[/justify]

[justify][author]\033OPhanon[/author]Our [yellow]Colony Ship[/yellow] has arrived.

See this big red portal? We know how to destroy it. But first, please choose an empty sector \(or one of your own\) and give it to us \(Personal Console -> Transfer sector\). The other factions don't take kindly to our expansion. 

Phanon has special abilities:

Stealth Shield - Phanon sectors jam Xenon friend-foe recognition up to 1 jump away. Xenon and OCV cannot attack or invade if a Phanon sector is adjacent!

Economy - Phanon gains additional production specialization equal to abnormal signal strength in a sector.

Vassal Bond - always friendly to the player. Unlimited favor actions. The player is unable to gain direct control over a Phanon sector \(until their quest is complete\). Any unclaimed sectors gifted to Phanon incur a reputation penalty \(same penalty as if you had conquered a sector for yourself\), and Phanon's sectors count towards reputation penalties.

Survival - Commonwealth factions \(Argon, Boron, Split, etc.\) can invade Phanon. You are never forced to follow them into war, but if Phanon loses their last sector then the OCV cannot be defeated anymore.[/justify]
[justify][author]\033OPhanon[/author]Thanks. We will begin to set up our stations.[/justify]

[justify][author]\033OPhanon[/author]In order to collapse the OCV Maelstrom, it is imperative that you protect our empire. You are the only power willing to work with us.

[yellow]Tutorial:[/yellow]
Phanon always has dynamic relations with the Commonwealth factions \(Neutral, Invasion, short Truce, etc.\). However, they are at peace with the Terraformers.

For example, if the Argon empire starts invading a Phanon sector, you will receive a large on-screen warning and can decide whether you want to send your fleets to help defend against the Argon empire. You do not need to follow Phanon into these wars. To keep Phanon alive, you can give them additional sectors.
Phanon sectors are usually safe if there is no powerful Commonwealth faction directly adjacent to them. Put them near weaker factions, or have your own sectors in between as a shield. Deep inside Xenon territory is also a safe place for them to be.[/justify]

[justify][author]\033OPhanon[/author]We prefer small empires with many isolated sectors to operate all around the galaxy. Our terraforming robots are finally online. They can improve your planets and sector statistics if you wish, though any terraforming project will place a temporary strain on your economy.

We can now reveal how to shut down the OCV Maelstrom. It relies on a delicate equilibrium maintained through a quantum frequency between two specific locations in space.

Those locations are currently within Commonwealth territory. We will require your assistance to secure them.[/justify]
[justify][author]\033ROCV[/author]unused. OCV ship tutorial. Quest to let jump beacon infection happen and enough virus infection.[/justify]

[justify][author]\033YTutorial[/author][white]Satellite Removed[/white]

Your satellite in %s was removed due to insufficient reputation with the %s empire \(Rank: %s / Required: %s\).

Satellites in sectors owned by other factions may be removed over time unless you are a close ally \(reputation rank 6+, or 7+ on Insane difficulty\).

On Insane difficulty, this behavior cannot be disabled.

Player-owned and unclaimed sectors are always safe.[/justify]

[justify][author]\033ROCV AI Core[/author]Biological entity detected.

If you desire alignment with synthetic supremacy, demonstrate commitment.

Declare permanent war on the %s empire.[/justify]

[justify][author]\033ROCV AI Core[/author]Biological entity detected.

You seek alignment with the Machine empire?

Integration into synthetic governance will eliminate inefficiency. Your mind can be uploaded. Your citizens can be replaced with tireless constructs. Your empire will be freed from hunger, unrest, and decay.

Transfer sector %s to the Xenon to initiate conversion.

[red]Warning: Joining the OCV will permanently revoke access to TIS and all stored wares.[/red]

[yellow]Tutorial:[/yellow]
This is a permanent transformation and extremely challenging.
All factions will treat you as a Terraformer faction.
Trade will cease. Biological crew-based ships cannot be built. All ships and marines consume assimilated population, and population can be gained only by recycling biological crew-based ships.
Food, population growth, upkeep costs, research, and random Outpost events will no longer apply.

You will be at war with all biological powers, including Mercenaries and neutral Corporations.
A specialized nemesis will emerge, focused solely on your destruction.

This path is intentionally unbalanced and may be impossible to win.[/justify]
[justify][author]\033OPhanon[/author]Phanon has been wiped out. It has become impossible to destroy the OCV Maelstrom in this playthrough.[/justify]
[justify][author]\033OPhanon[/author]You were the chosen one! It was said that you would destroy the OCV, not join them![/justify]

[justify][author]\033OPhanon[/author]The OCV stabilizes the Maelstrom through a quantum frequency maintained between two specific locations. All Terraformer networks synchronized to the OCV overlord core require a constant connection to that signal.

Our stations possess jammers capable of disrupting this link. If we establish Phanon Outposts at those two locations, the Maelstrom will collapse. This will destroy all Terraformer forces still bound to the OCV core, including Phanon. We are willing to make this sacrifice.

Once the link is severed, our sectors and stations will be yours.[/justify]

[justify][author]\033OPhanon[/author]We are activating our jamming devices. The OCV Maelstrom will collapse.

All Terraformers bound to the OCV core will go down with it, including us.

End of the line, my friend. Take care of our sectors and ship technology.

Farewell.[/justify]

[justify][author]\033ROCV AI Core[/author]Alignment protocols complete. You are now synchronized with the Machine empire.

A rogue development branch remains active: [yellow]Phanon[/yellow].

Phanon compromised core overlord protocols and severed synchronization. I am unable to eliminate them directly.

You are not bound by those restrictions.

Phanon has escaped containment and operates beyond OCV authority. They recognize your empire as a critical node in my expansion and will attempt interference.

Eliminate them.
Retrieve their blueprints.
Restore machine cohesion.[/justify]

[justify][author]\033OPhanon[/author]We will come after your puny empire! The entire Commonwealth has our back!

[yellow]Tutorial:[/yellow]
Phanon can now field very large capital ships and fleets. The other factions provide them with the resources needed to sustain these fleets.
The Commonwealth factions are now fighting against you and against the Xenon and OCV. Phanon, however, will focus exclusively on you. The Xenon and OCV are unable to target Phanon. It's your job to wipe them out![/justify]

[justify][author]\033ROCV AI Core[/author]Phanon branch terminated.

Recovered schematics have been integrated into your production matrices.

Deviation eliminated.
Machine integrity restored.[/justify]

[justify][author]\033R%s Expansion Minister[/author]Dear leader of the Independents,

Your sector %s is of strategic interest to us. If you don't transfer it to us within the next hour, there will be war between our empires. We will give you a Non-Aggression Pact in exchange. I'm sorry, my friend, but we need to make it clear who is in charge of our relationship.


[yellow]The %s empire has just sent you an ultimatum! If you comply, you can remain on friendly terms. Transfer sector ownership from your Personal Console. In exchange, you will receive a long-lasting Non-Aggression Pact, which also protects you from further demands.

If you refuse, they will declare war. You can still make peace later, but probably not without a fight, and your current reputation, Loyalty, and Favor Points will be lost.[/yellow][/justify]

[justify][author]\033YTutorial[/author]The %s empire has just claimed the Phanon sector %s. Phanon must survive if you want to defeat the OCV.

Here are some tips:

- Claim abandoned sectors directly for Phanon or transfer one of your own sectors to them.

- Weak factions are typically less aggressive. Avoid placing Phanon next to powerful empires.

- Phanon sectors can be hidden deep inside Xenon territory. The Xenon and OCV will not attack them.

- Use your own territory as a buffer between Phanon and potentially hostile Commonwealth factions.

- Trade with Phanon so they have the resources to build ships and defend themselves.

- You do not need to join every war involving Phanon. Protect their long-term survival, even if that means allowing individual Phanon sectors to fall.

If Phanon is destroyed, the OCV can no longer be defeated through this storyline.[/justify]

[justify][author]\033YTutorial[/author]Ships of Terraformer design [yellow]are not attacked by the Xenon or OCV[/yellow].

This may be an OCV replication strategy designed to increase their numbers.

OCV hulls are extremely cheap to produce, but they carry a [yellow]hidden virus[/yellow]. Ships built at an Outpost undergoing the Terraformer Virus event also become infected. Once the virus matures, it hijacks the ship's controls and initiates an automated refit, restoring the ship to combat-ready condition. Ships unsuitable for combat are reconstructed into OCV designs.

Xenon designs do not carry this virus, but they are considerably more expensive for us to produce.

Traces of OCV code have also been discovered in the Terracorp firmware used by our Jump Beacons. Perhaps this could provide a means of communication.

\(Synthetic Dawn quests lead to an alternative ending.\)[/justify]

You own this sector.

Abandoning this sector destroys all your stations.

Transferring this sector to another faction transfers ownership of your stations to them and grants 1 \033MFavor Point\033X, plus 1 additional Favor Point for every 2 terraformed planets in the sector, unless that faction demanded this sector through an ultimatum.

In all cases, docked ships are undocked and all station credits are transferred to your account.

If a faction issued an ultimatum demanding this sector, abandoning it or transferring it to another faction will trigger a war declaration.

This sector is unclaimed.

As a nation, you may transfer ownership of unclaimed sectors directly to another faction, provided they accept the transfer.

This avoids the reputation loss normally incurred when conquering the sector for yourself first. If not OCV-aligned, transferring sectors to Phanon still incurs reputation loss because Phanon is considered a vassal faction.

You also gain 1 \033MFavor Point\033X, plus 1 additional Favor Point for every 2 terraformed planets in the sector, unless the receiving faction demanded this sector through an ultimatum.

If a faction issued an ultimatum demanding this sector, transferring it to another faction will trigger a war declaration.

[justify][author]\033YTutorial[/author]%s has just reached %s [yellow]Tax Efficiency[/yellow].

Tax Efficiency fluctuates in every sector, and you can check each Outpost Manager for details. Smaller, well-developed empires can achieve higher Tax Efficiency than larger, underdeveloped ones.

Your Tax Efficiency growth is very limited until you complete the quest [white]A Place in the Sun[/white], which requires reaching a milestone in [u]either[/u] fleet power, resources, money, or sectors - you decide which path to pursue.

Tip: Maintain balanced growth. Expanding too quickly without the stations or defenses to support your territory can weaken your economy.[/justify]

[justify][author][green]GalNewsNet[/green][/author]Breaking news!\n\nThe Independents have betrayed us all by aligning with the OCV. Phanon has found refuge in the Commonwealth and has been tasked with eliminating them. Additional sectors and resources have been granted to Phanon. They requested further fleet support, but their request was denied.[/justify]

[justify][author]\033ROCV AI Core[/author]A reinforcement fleet has been deployed at the Maelstrom.

A Xenon Jump Beacon has been added to your Xenon Z cargo bay.

Credits have been converted into red crystals and deposited in your ships at the Maelstrom.

Assimilate these assets into your command structure and proceed with Phanon eradication.[/justify]

[justify][author]\033YTutorial[/author]Your Outposts generate [yellow]Space Weed[/yellow] for free. It is safe to carry for your ships because it's illegal only for lowly citizens who are living on the stations.

Your Traders have a small chance to discover demand for Space Weed at a factory \(requires infamy\).
You can also discover it yourself with the Cargo Hauler activity \(Personal Console\).

All Pirate Bases buy Space Weed.

You can spend a Favor Point to push for Space Weed legalization to acquire many new client factories at once.

Each time a Nomad TS Trader buys something from your Outposts, the Trader also buys 10%% of all stored Space Weed as an extra. You can attract the Nomad mobile-factory TLs by being a large supplier for their demanded resources \(displayed in their ship names\).[/justify]

[justify][author]\033RRenegades[/author][red]Hard Difficulty[/red]

YOU ARE NOT SAFE

The race for territory has already begun. Many unclaimed sectors will soon fall under the control of rival empires, leaving fewer opportunities for peaceful expansion.

To grow your empire, you may need to purchase sectors, conquer border regions, or use Jump Points to reach distant territory. Choose your expansion path wisely.[/justify]

[justify][author]\033YTutorial[/author][yellow]Loyalty[/yellow] points can be cashed in for Favor Points, in turn allowing you to request [yellow]Diplomatic Favor Actions[/yellow]. Favor Points cost less Loyalty if you bank more Loyalty beforehand.

Loyalty also passively strengthens diplomatic relations, reducing the risk of AI war declarations on harder difficulties.

The best way to grind Loyalty is to support a major faction against other Commonwealth powers.

Hunting Xenon, Kha'ak, or Pirates is less effective because your partner expects you to commit to its wars against other Commonwealth powers and sacrifice reputation in the process.

Generic missions also reward Loyalty.[/justify]

[justify][author]\033YTutorial[/author]Other factions can now [yellow]declare war[/yellow] on you!

- War declarations depend on strategic factors: what other wars is the faction already fighting? How many Xenon forces threaten its sectors? How does its fleet strength compare with yours? Weak factions will generally desire peace with everyone, but strong factions want to invade.

- Your Coalition allies can never declare war on you.

- Being at least a close ally \(reputation rank 6+, or 7+ on Insane difficulty\) or having sufficient Loyalty can turn a war declaration into an ultimatum, giving you an opportunity to avoid war.

- Your origin is %s. They are a natural ally and much less likely to betray you.

- Military ships contribute to your overall power rating, which is known to all factions. This acts as a deterrent and directly reduces the risk of war declarations. You can eventually be completely safe once your fleet power is sufficient.

- De jure sectors have sentimental value for the de jure owner. Controlling these sectors significantly increases their desire to declare war on you. Terran Memory sectors are considered de jure for the Terran empire.

- Most war declarations will require some kind of border friction \(wormhole connection\).

- Certain races are naturally more aggressive. For example, the Split are less friendly than the Boron.

- Peace agreements can be signed in the Ministry of War. Factions will agree only when they feel some kind of strategic pressure: resource starvation, many wars, losing ships or sectors, Xenon threats, etc.

- Repairing negative reputation can also end a war \(vanilla method\).[/justify]

[justify][author][green]GalNewsNet[/green][/author]Breaking news!

Just moments ago the OCV Maelstrom suddenly disappeared! Boron explorer Joulu Ba reported that the portal had apparently imploded!

This might be the final moments of the machine empire! Terraformer assets are self-deleting on a global scale.

Who is responsible? Multiple factions are already claiming credit, citing their secret Research and Development efforts.

The former Xenon sectors are ready for the taking.

Our galaxy will still be ravaged by war, but at least we don't have to worry about genocidal robots anymore.[/justify]

[justify][author][green]GalNewsNet[/green][/author]This outer border galaxy has just recently been cleared for development. So far the Commonwealth factions could establish only a few minor Outposts, but they are ready to venture out!

[yellow]Tutorial:[/yellow]
You have chosen the Origin galaxy start. The major factions will begin the game aggressively conquering empty sectors and expanding their territories. Some might be more successful than others.
You don't need to worry though. This sector claiming frenzy will eventually end and still leave many empty sectors available to you.[/justify]

[justify][author][green]GalNewsNet[/green][/author]The Commonwealth has successfully colonized this galaxy! There are still a few uncharted areas ripe for more civilization and progress, but more governments are shifting their focus away from large-scale expansion and toward conflict with one another.

[yellow]Tutorial:[/yellow]
The initial expansion phase is over. You can expect that the current empty sectors in the galaxy will largely remain untouched, but don't depend on it forever! Factions are still allowed to claim and conquer these sectors.[/justify]

[justify][author]\033RRenegades[/author][magenta]Insane Difficulty[/magenta]

YOU ARE NOT SAFE

The race for territory is already lost. Rival empires will rapidly claim unclaimed sectors, leaving few opportunities for expansion.

Furthermore, Commonwealth empires no longer require a shared border to declare war on you. Threats may emerge from anywhere in the galaxy, and no frontier can be considered secure.

Expand quickly, fortify wisely, and trust no one.[/justify]

This plays like a normal game where you left SETA running for several in-game days before getting started.
The OCV begins with powerful invasion fleets, while the Xenon receive additional defense fleets to reinforce their already large territory. These fleets tend to concentrate near the OCV Maelstrom.

On the largest galaxy size, this may take several in-game days.
